_: THE PRINCIPAL'S OWN CONFIRMATIONS. Two facts about a study can only be established by the principal and never inferred from the repository: whether it WENT THROUGH AUDIT, and whether TESTAHIL READ THAT AUDIT AND RESPONDED. Per instruction 09-09-2026: 'this is an activity that I have to confirm and then you add to the table.'
_why_this_file_exists: On 09-09-2026 both columns were filled by reading each study directory for an AUDIT_*.md and a *critique*.py|md, and eleven names came back audited and twelve responded. That was WRONG. A file existing is evidence that some document was written; it is not evidence that the audit the principal commissions took place, nor that the house answered it. The correct answer was ONE name. Inference was substituted for confirmation, which is the same failure as a study attesting its own gate [R-ENF-01] — the claim was made by the thing that wanted it to be true.
_rule: A row is added here ONLY on the principal's explicit word, quoting it. Nothing else may write to this file, and no gate or board may fill these two columns from the repository.

_everything_else: UNCONFIRMED. Not 'no' — unconfirmed. The distinction matters: a name absent from this file has not been ruled either way, and a board must show it blank rather than negative.
_internal_qc_acceptance: A THIRD FACT ONLY THE PRINCIPAL CAN ESTABLISH, added 13-09-2026 on his instruction: whether he ACCEPTS a study's open internal-QC findings and clears it to proceed. This is not the QC verdict and does not overwrite one. A gate says what an auditor found; this says what the principal decided to do about it. Keeping the two apart is the whole point -- a verdict edited to say 'nothing found' when the findings are listed two pages below it stops being worth anything the next time anyone relies on one, and the principal is the person it would stop being worth anything to.
